Model-generated explanation — professional review required.

The CMA uses flat adjustment rates ($110 / sf, $12k per bedroom, $15k per bathroom) that assume linear value contributions and ignore potential interaction effects; the evidence notes that "Bedroom and square‑footage adjustments may double‑count related value" and that these rates are user‑defined, not derived from the sample (cma-01). This raises uncertainty about the validity of the adjustments for properties with differing layouts or quality levels. [cma-01]

Weighting is based on inverse distance, sale age, and relative size, yet the CMA does not model lot size, school zones, concessions, or condition, all of which can materially affect value. The comparable list (property‑02 – property‑08) lacks any indicators of these factors, so the weighted mean may be biased by unobserved attributes. [property-02] [property-03] [property-04] [property-05] [property-06] [property-07] [property-08]

The 0 % monthly trend assumption treats the market as static, which conflicts with the disclaimer that “trend is an explicit user assumption, not a learned coefficient.” Without calibrated trend data, the range may misrepresent current market dynamics. [cma-01]

All property and market evidence in this workspace is fictional demonstration data.
